Title: GET /api/v1/auth/me returns null created_at/updated_at/last_login_at for a user that has real values
Environment: Local Docker Compose install, ENV=development, api image built from current working-tree source; verified 2026-09-02
Preconditions: Logged in as a user with a real created_at/updated_at/last_login_at (any account that has previously logged in).
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in via POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials.
2. GET /api/v1/auth/me.
3. Separately, GET /api/v1/users and locate the same user id in the returned array.
4. Compare created_at/updated_at/last_login_at between the two responses for the identical user id.
Expected Result: Both endpoints return the same, correct, non-null created_at/updated_at/last_login_at values for the same user, since both read the same underlying row.
Actual Result: GET /api/v1/auth/me returns created_at=null, updated_at=null, last_login_at=null. GET /api/v1/users, for the identical user id at the same instant, returns real ISO-8601 timestamps for all three fields. Reproduced twice in a row (not a timing race).
Notes: Root cause located: backend/app/api/auth.py:128-137 constructs UserRead manually inside the /me handler and only passes id/email/display_name/role/is_active, omitting the three optional datetime fields declared on backend/app/schemas/auth.py:24-34 (UserRead), which silently default to None instead of raising a validation error. GET /users evidently builds UserRead from the ORM object directly (from_attributes=True), which is why it returns correct values for the identical row. Low customer impact (role/identity/is_active — the fields most consumers of /me actually need — are correct); any UI surface that sources 'member since' or 'last login' display data from /me specifically (rather than from /users) would show blank/incorrect values.
